title: CLI personal-tune workflow journal
body:
Summary:
This is a personal sketch for a CLI-first, local-first personal fine-tuning + evaluation flow. Goal: make it trivial for engineers to prototype fine-tune runs, inspect checkpoints, run tiny evals, and iterate on prompts/labels without pushing to the hosted training infra. Focus on ergonomics, clear defaults, and lightweight telemetry to guide suggestions (e.g., recommended batch size, quant/profile).

Why: I want quick turn-around loops when experimenting with prompt-template-level tuning or small adapter runs. Hosted infra is heavy and opaque for quick cycles. If the CLI can provide consistent local behavior that mirrors production transform steps, it will speed up iteration and reduce waste.

Principles:
- Minimal friction: single binary, tiny local deps, reproducible configs.
- Mirror production: same preprocess, tokenization, and eval hooks used by Redwood Optimize where possible.
- Visibility: clear local logs for token count, expected cost estimate if run in cloud, and per-step diffs.
- Safe defaults: caps on local batch size, disk usage, and telemetry opt-in prompt at first run.

User flow (sketch):
1) init project: redwood-cli tune init --name my-cust-qa
2) add data: redwood-cli tune ingest data.csv --schema prompt,answer,meta
3) quick-sim: redwood-cli tune simulate --n 10  # runs tokenization + fake batches to estimate cost
4) local run: redwood-cli tune run --profile small-adapter --steps 200 --target ./runs/exp1
5) eval: redwood-cli tune eval --checkpoint ./runs/exp1/ckpt.pt --evalset test.jsonl --metrics rouge,acc
6) publish (optional): redwood-cli tune publish --checkpoint ... --target hosted/dedicated

Command shape examples (notes):
- Command names intentionally short, verbs first.
- Flags are long-form with sensible defaults.

redwood-cli tune init --name <id> --model rdx-1-small --tokenizer auto
redwood-cli tune ingest <file.csv|dir/> --format csv|jsonl --schema "prompt:text,answer:text,split:train|val|test,source:str"
redwood-cli tune simulate [--n N] [--seq-len 1024]  # tokenization + batching dry-run
redwood-cli tune run --profile {small-adapter,linear-probe,full-ft} --steps N --batch-size B --lr LR --device cpu|gpu
redwood-cli tune checkpoint inspect ./runs/exp1/ckpt.pt --weights-summary

Config sketch (YAML-ish as string example):
project: my-cust-qa
model: rdx-1-small
profile: small-adapter
dirs:
  data: ./data
  runs: ./runs
training:
  steps: 2000
  batch_size: 8
  microbatch: 2
  lr: 1e-4
  gradient_accum: 1
  device: auto
preprocess:
  tokenizer: default
  seq_len: 1024
  normalize_unicode: true
eval:
  metrics: [accuracy,exact_match]
  eval_batch: 32
telemetry:
  opt_in: null  # null => prompt on first run; accepts yes/no
notes: |
  - default profile 'small-adapter' maps to LoRA-style adapters with 4-bit quantized weights when running on GPU.
  - 'simulate' uses the same tokenizer to surface token distribution and suggested batch sizes.

Local server API shape (for interactive UI / web-preview):
(HTTP JSON)
POST /v1/local-tune/start
  body: {"project_id": "str", "config": "yaml-string-or-json", "run_name": "str"}
Response: {"run_id": "str", "status": "queued", "port": 51823}

GET /v1/local-tune/<run_id>/status -> {"status": "running|done|failed", "progress": "0-100", "metrics": {"loss": "float"}, "current_checkpoint": "path"}

GET /v1/local-tune/<run_id>/inspect?step=100 -> {"batches_simulated": 10, "avg_tokens": 78, "token_histogram": "[[0,100],[1,500]]"}

Note: responses are intentionally small strings/ints to keep local server lightweight. We keep long objects behind file endpoints (e.g., /artifact/<id>).

Telemetry event examples (only emitted if user opt-in):
- event: tune.simulate.run -> {project_id, n_examples, seq_len, suggested_batch}
- event: tune.run.started -> {project_id, profile, device_hint, estimated_peak_ram}
- event: tune.eval.completed -> {project_id, metrics, eval_time_s}
These are intentionally coarse; no data payload includes raw prompt/answer contents.

ASCII flow diagram (quick):
[user CLI] -> [local preprocessor] -> [simulator] -> [trainer] -> [checkpoint dir] -> [local eval harness]
            |                                                   ^                      |
            `-> (optional upload) -> [hosted ingestion] ---------'

Implementation experiments done so far (notes):
- Proof-of-concept uses a lightweight python runner (click + uvicorn) and tiny adapter code. Local run on M1 with 2GB per batch simulated OK for 200 steps.
- simulate command surfaced that many rows had >900 tokens; we added auto-trim suggestion to warn about seq_len mismatch.
- 'inspect' shows tokenization differences between model tokenizers (important to mirror prod tokenization exactly).

Open questions / TODOs:
- UX: Should 'simulate' be part of 'init' or explicit separate command? I prefer explicit, but maybe auto-run with --auto-sim flag.
- Safety: Should local run detect corporate data patterns and warn about upload? (simple regex PII detector?)
- Packaging: create a small binary bundle vs pip package? Binary reduces dependency friction for non-Python engineers.
- Integration: tie the 'publish' step to Redwood Console's model catalog and show diff (local vs hosted transforms).
- Metrics: pick a small default eval set sampler to provide a quick 'smoke' metric after 100 steps.

Notes to self for next pass:
- Add a 'dry-quant' step to estimate memory for quant profiles (4-bit vs 8-bit).
- Align tokenizer and normalization with hosted preprocess (copy code reference: infra/preprocess/tokenizer.py, TODO link once PR exists).
- Draft a short help text for each CLI command with examples that use tiny toy datasets.

Quick links / refs (local):
- Jira: INF-1284 (linked above)
- local branch: feature/cli-local-tune (PR link above)

Rough prioritization (what I plan to implement next):
1) simulate -> robust token histogram + recommended batch size logic (high value)
2) run --profile small-adapter with auto-lora init
3) checkpoint inspect (weights summary + small diff against base model)
4) local eval smoke runner (quick metrics after short run)

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally rough; will convert to a proper spec once simulate + run prototypes are stable.
short_summary: Personal scratchpad for a CLI-first local fine-tune + eval workflow: commands, config sketch, API shape, telemetry notes, experiments, and TODOs
